status: Senate reported bill out of committee to 14th Order for amendment on 2025-03-26; no further Senate action recorded; the 2025 session has since concluded with no enactment, so the bill is dead.
key_provisions: Would have revised provisions for the Idaho information technology equipment sales tax exemption.

status: Signed by Governor 2020-03-30; Session Law Chapter 335; effective 2020-07-01.
key_provisions: Created Idaho's data-center sales and use tax exemption for eligible server equipment and new data center facilities. Current Idaho Code 63-3622VV requires at least $250 million in capital investment within 5 years and at least 30 new jobs within 2 years after operations begin.

sponsors: House Revenue and Taxation Committee (committee print); Idaho Conservation League identifies Rep. Chris Bruce as the principal sponsor
status: Introduced 2026-02-09; reported printed and referred to House Revenue & Taxation 2026-02-10; no further action recorded; died at 2026 sine die.
key_provisions: Would have narrowed data center tax exemptions, added electricity cost-recovery and water-notice qualification criteria, prevented stacking with the new capital investment property tax exemption, and added a 2036 sunset review. Not a moratorium bill.

status: Introduced 2026-02-24; reported printed and referred to State Affairs 2026-02-25; no further action recorded; died at 2026 sine die.
key_provisions: Earlier House draft on the same subject as H0911 ('Public Utility - Amends and adds to existing law to provide for new large loads'); received only a committee referral and was not advanced, apparently superseded by H0911.

status: Introduced 2026-03-04; reported printed and referred to House Revenue & Taxation 2026-03-05; no further action recorded; died at 2026 sine die.
key_provisions: Similar tax exemption revision bill for data centers, including sales tax and new capital investment property tax provisions. Not a moratorium bill.

sponsors: House Ways and Means Committee; floor sponsors Rep. Britt Raybould and Sen. C. Scott Burtenshaw
status: Passed House 58-10-2 (2026-03-20) and Senate 32-1-2 (2026-03-31); signed by Governor 2026-04-02; Session Law Chapter 291; effective 2026-07-01.
key_provisions: Adds Idaho Code 42-252. Data centers beginning construction on or after 2026-07-01 may not use water for cooling as a consumptive use unless supplied by a municipal, water district, or water and sewer district water system. Legislative findings state data center water demand conflicts with local public interest, water conservation, and local watershed economies for water-right review purposes.

sponsors: House Ways and Means Committee print; Idaho Conservation League identifies Rep. Chris Bruce, Sen. Lori Den Hartog, and Rep. John Gannon as named sponsors
status: Passed House 68-0-2 on 2026-03-23; passed Senate as amended 34-0-1 on 2026-04-01; returned to House and referred to Revenue & Taxation for concurrence recommendation on 2026-04-02; no concurrence vote or further action is recorded thereafter, so the bill died for lack of House concurrence at 2026 sine die.
key_provisions: Would have limited sales tax exemption eligibility to 20 years, applied server-equipment-only treatment to data centers commencing construction on or after 2026-04-01, required utility cost recovery for new qualifying data centers, required water-consumption notice to local water providers and IDWR, required annual forgone-sales-tax reports, and required 5-year reports on jobs, investment, electricity impacts, and water impacts. Not a moratorium bill.

status: Passed House 65-3-2 (2026-03-20); passed Senate 34-1-0 (2026-03-30); signed by Governor 2026-04-10; Session Law Chapter 335; effective 2026-07-01 via emergency clause.
key_provisions: Adds Idaho Code 61-335, titled 'New Large Load and Ratepayer Protection.' Defines a 'new large load' as a service-entrance load increase of 50 MW or more within a rolling 60-month period under a contract entered on or after 2026-07-01 (squarely covers data centers). Requires a PUC-approved service contract before a utility may serve such a load, including a commission 'no harm test'; makes the new large load responsible for its full cost of service (generation, transmission, substation, distribution); bars load-splitting to evade the threshold; requires financial security against stranded costs; and directs the commission to review rates in each general rate case to keep other ratepayers' bills from rising because of the new load.

status: Introduced 2026-03-04; reported printed and referred to State Affairs 2026-03-05; no further action recorded; died at 2026 sine die.
key_provisions: Senate companion draft on the same subject as H0911 and H0756 ('Public Utilities - Adds to existing law to provide for new large loads'); received only a committee referral and was not advanced.
